messages.subject: Harrow v Brevdale - clause 12 and the clause 7 carve-out
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

I've been through the Supply Agreement. Clause 12 caps aggregate liability at 150% of the price paid in the preceding 12 months. Harrow paid £611,200 for the relevant deliveries, so on Brevdale's reading the cap is £916,800. BUT clause 12 has a carve-out: 'nothing in the Supply Agreement limits liability for breach of clause 7'. Clause 7 is the conformity warranty - exactly what's been breached.

My view is the carve-out is unqualified and knocks out the cap for these breaches. Brevdale will say it only carves out the clause 9.2 replacement remedy. Worth getting Harriet's view early.

James
